# Retained ScenePilot engine

Generated by `node scripts/vendor-scenepilot.mjs` from the local ScenePilot source repository `tcc-operations/repos/scenepilot-studio-badass`, revision `277f1544f7ac1e6e24426571c171cc21d3ea31ea`. The bundle retains its actual cut parser/diagnostics, title appearance, timeline conversion, media relink and clip trim functions. There are no bundled third-party runtime modules. Normal Hole builds copy this checked-in bundle and do not require the source repository.

The connected editor supports native `.cut` / `.scenepilot.json` documents up to 32 MiB, title text/timing changes and ordinary unlocked clip trims. It preserves the raw native document, including unknown fields and `proState`, while validating through the native parser. Reversed, time-remapped and transform-keyframed clips require the full studio. Original input versions remain in Hole.

Media access requires explicit Hole asset/version grants. The host receives `editorState.mediaLinks` entries `{sourceId, assetId, versionId}`; `sourceId` is a native asset id or `__main__` for `mainAsset`. At most 63 entries are accepted. These sources have read-only grants. Missing, mismatched and ungranted media remains explicit; native source paths are never fetched. MIME kind and supplied byte size are checked, not a content hash or semantic identity.

The preview shows a granted original source and native title appearance. It does not render a full composition, effects stack, audio mix or exported movie. Full ScenePilot remains accessible through the original tool route. This bounded integration does not claim complete studio parity.

Wave 14 refresh adds only named exports of retained `splitVideoTrackClip` (`lib/video-track-edit.ts`) and `sourceTimeForCut` (`lib/pro-editor.ts`), from the same unchanged revision. Existing exports remain. SHA-256 of `engine.js`: `e15f1d6d61e4e7beff7f9a122fd7f31bed198ae1c38e4d9dba5b1eebc6e79429`. The source is retained owned application code, not a newly licensed public library; no root LICENSE grant was found or invented. The generator retains available legal comments. No model, media, external runtime or model notice from the source repository is bundled by this extraction.

The connected surface now also supports native splits (at most 200 clips, strictly interior points leaving at least 0.04 seconds on each side), bounded Undo and native `.cut` copy export. Matching raw primary/legacy clip representations must agree before mutation. Source inspection uses the actual retained source clock and pauses at that source timestamp; it supports ordinary 0.1–8× clips within one-hour cuts. Linked sources remain exact read-only versions, bounded at 32 MiB each / 64 MiB aggregate; decoded inspection rejects edges over 2048 or four million pixels. Decoder allocation happens before dimension admission, so this is not a browser-process memory guarantee. Exported native cuts reference media rather than embedding it and record exact loaded links in provenance.
